numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE FROM THE RIGHT-FIELD / FIRST-BASE SIDE TOWARD THE THIRD-BASE / LEFT-FIELD SIDE on every tier. LOW numbers = right field and first base side. HIGH numbers = third base side and left field. This holds for the lower Promenade bowl (1 at the right-field foul pole, 8-10 at the first-base dugout, 13-18 behind home plate, 19-21 at the third-base dugout, 22-28 down the left-field line, 29-32 behind the left-field wall), for the Legends 200 level (201-204 right field, 207-211 first base, 219-222 third base, 223-228 left field), and for the Vista 300 level (302-305 right field, 306-310 first base, 311-318 behind the plate, 319-322 third base, 323-327 left field). IMPORTANT NON-MONOTONIC WRAP IN THE LOWER BOWL: after section 32 (behind the left-field wall) the lower-bowl numbering appears to continue around through center field and land back in RIGHT field. RateYourSeats' March-2026 Home Run Porch page states the porch (134-141) is 'above the right field outfield seats' and that 'the lower right field sections (34-40) [are] located directly beneath the porch', and Ballparks of Baseball independently states 'Two levels of seats are located above the right field fence with limited seating located behind the left field fence.' So 34-40 are RIGHT-field outfield sections under the Home Run Porch, NOT a continuation past left field. Sections 33 and 37 do not exist in the ticketed index. The Home Run Porch tier (134-141) is right-field-only and does not run through the infield.

accessibility.summary: Wheelchair-accessible and semi-ambulatory seats with operable armrests are located on ALL ballpark levels, generally at the TOP of most sections (which matches the RateYourSeats row data, where accessible rows are labeled 'WC' and the section entrance is at row WC). One companion/escort may sit with a guest with a disability in designated accessible seating; folding chairs can be provided. Eight public elevators serve all seating levels, located primarily at the 3rd Base, PNC Club and 1st Base Dugout Club entrances; ramps are available as an alternative. Electrical outlets for medical devices are provided in designated seating areas on the Promenade, Legends and Vista Levels. Braille and tactile signage throughout; closed captioning on the Legends Level ribbon display; sensory kits and a sensory room for neurodivergent guests on the Legends Level (5th floor). Wheelchair transport to and from seats can be requested at entrances or by texting 305-480-4999; Guest Experience is reachable at 305-480-1300. Accessible parking is first-come first-served in all four parking garages and two surface lots (East Lot 2 and East Lot 3), with a placard or disability plate required. Miami-Dade Paratransit drop-off/pick-up is at NW 6th Street & NW 16th Avenue. Rideshare pickup/drop-off is East Lot 1, 1380 NW 6th Street. General gates open 90 minutes before first pitch; the Marlins Member Express Entrance is at West Plaza Gate 1 and the Home Plate Entrance. CAVEAT: the MLB.com Access Guide for Guests With Disabilities (https://mlb.com/marlins/ballpark/disability-access-guide) could not be fetched directly (https://www.mlb.com/marlins/ballpark/accessibility returned empty); the elevator, gate, parking and paratransit details above come from a WebSearch summary of that MLB.com page plus the SeatSecrets guide, and should be re-verified against the club page before publication.

row_seat_conventions: MIXED LETTERS AND NUMBERS, varying by level and by section. Promenade / lower bowl infield sections use lettered rows first, then numbered rows: section 12 and section 18 are 'A-E, 1-27' with the section entrance at row 27; section 40 is 'A-G, 1-12' with the entrance at row 12. Some lower-bowl corner sections are numbers only and do not start at 1: section 1 is 'rows 9-30' with the entrance at row 30. The small left-field strip sections use short number-only ranges plus an accessible row: section 29 is 'rows 1-8, WC' with the entrance at row WC. HOME RUN PORCH: section 134 is 'rows 1-5, WC' (entrance at row WC); section 141 is 'rows 1-16' (entrance at row 8). LEXUS LEGENDS 200 LEVEL: sections 211 and 219 are 'rows 1-10, WC' with the entrance at row WC; the Legends Platinum review states no section has more than 10 rows and sections 202-204 have only 8 rows. VISTA 300 LEVEL: mixed - section 315 is 'A-C, 1-16' (entrance at row 3); section 327 is 'A-K, 1-9' (entrance at row K). DUGOUT CLUB (FL1-FL3, FL9-FL11): rows AA through DD, i.e. every seat within the first four rows of the field. BULLPEN BAR & GRILL reserved seating: its own internal sections 1-3, rows A-D. ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL: 'WC' - RateYourSeats consistently phrases it 'Rows in Section N are labeled 1-10, WC' and 'An entrance to this section is located at Row WC', i.e. the wheelchair row is at the top of the section at the concourse entrance. No 'WCH', 'VWC' or AC-suffix convention was found at this park.
seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the field/field/stage, lower number seats are on the right" - RateYourSeats renders the sentence with the '/field/stage' artifact because the page carries Baseball/Football/Concert tabs; the baseball reading is 'When looking towards the field, lower number seats are on the right.' VERIFIED IDENTICAL ON ELEVEN SECTION PAGES, one per level: lower bowl 1, 12, 18, 29, 40; Home Run Porch 134, 141; Legends 211, 219; Vista 315, 327. NO CONTRADICTING SOURCE FOUND. Therefore seat 1 is on the RIGHT as you face the field, i.e. seat numbers increase from right to left when looking at the field, in every section checked at every tier. URLs: https://www.rateyourseats.com/loandepot-park/seating/sections/1 , /12 , /18 , /29 , /40 , /134 , /141 , /211 , /219 , /315 , /327
known_obstructions: PROTECTIVE NETTING (official, installed for the 2019 season and still the configuration described by the club): MLB.com, verbatim - 'the netting will be 30 feet high at the ends of each dugout, and taper down each foul line to the ends of Section 3 in right field, and FL11 in left field.' The netting is knotless Dyneema, 30 percent thinner than traditional netting; portions are adjustable with autograph access points along the entire length of both dugouts plus four areas down the first-base line and three down the third-base line. RateYourSeats fan feedback (attached to sections 12 and 18), verbatim: 'There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 8-21. The height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section.' A fan in section 18 row 8 wrote 'Great seats almost behind home plate. You do have to look through the net...'. A separate search summary attributed to the same MLB netting story reported netting 'covers Sections 4 - 10 & 19 - 25' - that phrasing does NOT appear in the MLB.com article text as fetched, so treat it as unverified. OTHER: RateYourSeats flags 'Obstructed/Limited Views' as a section insight for sections 1, 134 and 141. A fan review in section 1 row 21: 'The yellow foul pole is distracting when looking at the outfield.' Sections 134 and 141 are additionally flagged 'Behind/Side Stage (most shows)' for concerts. FOOTBALL-ONLY (not applicable to baseball): 'For football games at Marlins Park, right field sections can not see the entire field. Obstructed sections include Field sections 1-4, outfield sections 134-141 and sections 201-204 and 302-305.' VIDEOBOARD SIGHTLINE: the main videoboard (101 ft x 51 ft) is above the right-centerfield stands, so right-field-side seats struggle to see it; the best videoboard views are from the third-base side.
uncertain: VENUE NAME STYLING: sources disagree on capitalization. MLB.com and Ballparks of Baseball use 'loanDepot park' (lower-case l, lower-case p); Ballparks of Baseball explicitly notes 'the l is not capitalized in the name'. RateYourSeats uses 'loanDepot Park' (capital P) in headings but 'loanDepot park' in some captions. Wikipedia's article title is 'LoanDepot Park'. Recommend rendering 'loanDepot park' as the club does, but be aware of the split.

RENAME HISTORY: the building opened in 2012 as Marlins Park and was renamed loanDepot Park in March 2021. Much of the RateYourSeats content and nearly all its photo filenames still say 'Marlins Park', and some expert reviews still refer to 'Marlins Park' in body text. This is stale wording, not a second venue. No further rename found as of August 2026; 2026 Marlins home games are listed at loanDepot Park.

DUGOUT SIDE - UNRESOLVED CONFLICT, HIGHEST-PRIORITY ITEM TO RE-VERIFY. Ballparks of Baseball states '-Home Dugout: Third Base'. RateYourSeats' own Promenade Level Infield review places the Marlins dugout in front of sections 19-21 and the visitors dugout in front of sections 8-10 - and 19-21 are on the third base side under the confirmed numbering direction. RateYourSeats' seating-guide caption says the '3B (Marlins) side of the field'. BUT RateYourSeats' Dugout Club page (last verified March 2026) says the opposite: 'First Base Side (Sections F1-F3): These seats sit on the Marlins dugout side of the field' and 'Third Base Side (Sections F9-F11): These seats sit near the visiting team dugout'. MLB.com's Dugout Clubs page names 'The First and Third Base Dugout Clubs' but never assigns a team to either, so it does not settle it. Recommended value is THIRD BASE (three-plus sources vs one), but do not present it as certain without a fresh official confirmation.

LOWER-BOWL WRAP / SECTIONS 34-40: RateYourSeats' March-2026 Home Run Porch page places 34-40 in RIGHT field beneath the porch, and Ballparks of Baseball independently says 'Two levels of seats are located above the right field fence with limited seating located behind the left field fence', which fits. However RateYourSeats' older Bullpen Outfield review says 'sections 38-39 are just behind the visiting bullpen in LEFT field' and 'Sections 29-31 ... behind the Marlins bullpen in left field', implying 29-40 are all left field. Both cannot be true. Recommended reading: 29-32 = the small strip behind the LEFT field wall (short row ranges, e.g. 29 is rows 1-8), 34-40 = the larger RIGHT field outfield deck under the Home Run Porch (rows A-G, 1-12). Verify against the club seat map before publishing anything that names a field for 34-40.

BULLPEN OWNERSHIP CONFLICT: RateYourSeats' expert review says the MARLINS bullpen is behind sections 29-31, while RateYourSeats' own fan-feedback item on section 29 says 'The Visitor Bullpen is Below Sections 29-31'. Ballparks of Baseball supports the expert review (pool behind the left field fence 'next to the Marlins bullpen'). A section 40 fan note says 'The Marlins Bullpen is to the Left of Section 40', which does not fit a right-field section 40 with the Marlins bullpen in left field. Recommended: Marlins bullpen = left field behind 29-31; visiting bullpen = right field behind 38-39 and beneath the Home Run Porch.

MISSING SECTION NUMBERS: 33 and 37 are absent from the lower bowl; 212-218 are absent from the 200 level; 301 is absent from the 300 level; FL12 and FL13 are absent from the field level. None of these appear in the RateYourSeats venue section index or in A View From My Seat's section list. No source states what occupies those gaps except the 200-level gap (suites and press behind home plate). Do not invent sections to fill them.

FL14, FL15 and FL16 appear in the RateYourSeats section index (under URLs /sections/fl_14, /fl_15, /fl_16) but no consulted source states where they are or whether they are sold for Marlins games. Their thumbnails reuse 2016 'Marlins-Park-Section-15/16-Row-A' images. They are included in sections[] because they are in the venue index, but their location is UNKNOWN and they may be an artifact.

CONCERT-ONLY SECTIONS: RateYourSeats groups concert floor seating under a single 'Field Seats for Concerts' page (/loandepot-park/seating/field-seats) that enumerates no individual section IDs, so no concert-only section names could be extracted. concert_only_sections is therefore empty rather than guessed. Note that sections 134 and 141 carry a concert-specific 'Behind/Side Stage (most shows)' warning but are ordinary baseball sections.

BULLPEN BAR & GRILL uses its own internal 'Sections 1-3, Rows A-D' which collide by name with lower-bowl sections 1-3 down the right field line. If the generator keys on bare section strings this is a real collision risk.
CAPACITY: 37,442 vs 36,742 (see capacity field). The 36,742 figure comes only from a search summary of Wikipedia, which could not be fetched directly.

COMPASS ORIENTATION: no source states which way the batter faces. Only Ballparks of Baseball's statement that the open roof 'sits behind the first base grandstand on the west side of the ballpark' gives any bearing. batter_faces is recorded as UNKNOWN rather than derived.

ROOF BEHAVIOUR: Ballparks of Baseball states the three-panel retractable roof opens or closes in 13 minutes and parks behind the first base grandstand on the west side; retractable glass panels behind left field (six panels, 240 ft x 60 ft combined) open or close in eight minutes. When the roof is closed the ballpark is air-conditioned. No source consulted gives the club's current rule for when the roof is opened or closed.

VISTA LEVEL AVAILABILITY: RateYourSeats states the Vista Level 'is often closed to fans due to lower attendance levels' for many regular-season Marlins games, opening mainly for marquee events. 300-level sections may therefore be unsellable on a given date.
PLAYING SURFACE / DIMENSIONS (for context, from Ballparks of Baseball): Shaw synthetic turf B1K since 2020; dimensions 340-L, 384-LC, 400-C, 387-RC, 335-R.
